newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs face correction, aim for 132.30.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs face correction, aim for 132.30.

text.p: September BTPs face the threat of a correction on Friday and may test 132.30 before bouncing back to new highs, technical analysts said.

"We certainly should see a correction today due to the overbought conditions yesterday," said Daniele Castelnuovo, analyst at Banca Euromobiliare in Milan. "I expect a test of 132.50, with a further support level around 132.30."

By 0738 GMT, September BTPs were up 26 basis points at 132.90. The Relative Strength Index was at 66.6 percent, down from 70.1 percent on Thursday. A reading over 70 percent indicates an overbought market.
Castelnuovo said he expected the market to bounce back on short covering once preliminary Italian inflation data due later was out of the way.
Guenter Redeker, technical analyst at Chase here, said Thursday's correction had lent BTPs a slightly bearish tone, as the market pierced Elliott support at 132.57.
"We saw a relatively sharp decline yesterday and just broke 132.57 to get to 132.55 which gave the market a bit of a bearish touch," he said.
"Now it's possible to test 132.14 to 132.02 before we get back up again."
Redeker put initial resistance at 133.15, followed by Thursday's high at 133.70.
"After that, there's trendline resistance at 134.14," he said.

By 0804 GMT, September Eurolira was up one basis point at 93.44. Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said in a note that as the contrct could not confirm the gains above 93.49, it would look for a test of support near the 93.39 congestion area.
